subject: CHEMISTRY

source_item.source_locator: NCERT Class IX Science Exemplar - Unit 2 Q35
source_item.stem: Iron filings and sulphur were mixed together and divided into two parts, A and B. Part A was heated strongly while Part B was not heated. Dilute hydrochloric acid was added to both parts and evolution of gas was seen in both cases. How will you identify the gases evolved?
source_item.canonical_answer: Part A gives hydrogen sulphide; part B gives hydrogen. Hydrogen sulphide has a characteristic rotten-egg odour; hydrogen is identified by the pop test.

help.text: The target is not merely to name two gases; you must connect each part to identifying evidence.
Treat Part A and Part B as two separate evidence chains. Do not combine them.
Use a two-row table: Part | what material is present before HCl | gas | identifying observation/test.
A gas identity is an inference; it must be supported by the observation or test used to identify it.
Start with Part A: strong heating makes iron and sulphur react before HCl is added. Then handle Part B separately.
Part A leads to hydrogen sulphide and Part B leads to hydrogen. Now supply the identification evidence for each without mixing the two chains.
See the complete worked solution below.
Verify that each gas identity is paired with its own evidence and that the heated/unheated branches were never merged.

full_solution: For Part A, strong heating causes iron and sulphur to form iron sulphide; with dilute HCl the evolved gas is hydrogen sulphide, identified by its characteristic foul/rotten-egg odour (and the governed marking point also records blackening with lead acetate). For Part B, the unheated mixture still contains iron; iron with dilute HCl evolves hydrogen, identified by the pop test. The answer is valid because each chemical inference is tied to the correct branch and its own identifying evidence.
verify_reflect: Can you point to the exact observation/test supporting each gas identity? If the gas names were removed, could you reconstruct them from the two evidence chains rather than from memory?
